item.title: IBM is tripling the number of Gen Z entry-level jobs after finding the limits of AI adoption
item.description: Gen Z jobs aren’t dead yet: $240 billion tech giant IBM says it’s rewriting entry-level jobs—and tripling down on its hiring of young talent.

item.title: Microsoft AI chief gives it 18 months—for all white-collar work to be automated by AI
item.description: Mustafa Suleyman believes current AI computational power will only accelerate, disrupting every kind of work you do “sitting down at a computer.”

item.title: Top analyst warns the economy is figuring out how to grow without creating new jobs, leaving a major vulnerability
item.description: The economy will grow because of higher productivity, aided in part by AI, says Michael Pearce of Oxford Economics. But people aren’t core to that story.

item.title: Bank of America lifts Moynihan’s pay 17% to $41 million for 2025
item.description: A year ago, Moynihan’s compensation was increased 21% to $35 million after the bank was able to boost its earnings.

item.title: Analog-obsessed Gen Zers are buying $40 app blockers to limit their social media use and take a break from the ‘slot machine in your pocket’
item.description: App-blocking devices like Bloom and Brick promise to improve focus and decrease compulsive phone checks by making social media harder to access.

item.title: Trump says regime change in Iran that ousts Islamic clerics ‘would be the best thing that could happen’ as another carrier heads to Mideast
item.description: Trump said the USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, is being sent from the Caribbean Sea to the Mideast.

item.title: Exclusive: The Walton family–funded PE firm that owns Rapha Cycling Club presses pause on all new investments
item.description: RZC Investments, the private equity firm of Walmart heirs Tom and Steuart Walton, said it was still “actively” managing its current portfolio.

item.title: Marc Andreessen made a dire software prediction 15 years ago. Now it’s happening in a way nobody imagined
item.description: The billionaire venture capitalist explained why software would eat the world in 2011. He had no idea.

item.title: Why Singapore’s prime minister gave DBS and Grab a shout-out during the country’s budget speech
item.description: Lawerence Wong called on Singapore's companies to adopt AI “comprehensively”, and described DBS and Grab as firms "moving decisively on AI transformation."

item.title: OpenAI’s Codex and Anthropic’s Claude spark coding revolution as developers say they’ve abandoned traditional programming
item.description: New releases from OpenAI and Anthropic sparked an existential crisis among coders, but many engineers say they stopped coding months ago.
